settings.text: Discover how The Glass Railing Store has been delivering exceptional service to our customers, thanks to our dedicated and knowledgeable team and their love our glass railing products.

settings.question: Do the products come with a warranty?
settings.answer: Yes — Glass panels are guaranteed to be free of manufacturing defects with a lifetime warranty, and hardware comes with a 10-year no-rust promise, utilizing marine-grade stainless steel.

settings.question: What is the hardware made of?
settings.answer: Our hardware is made from 2205 marine grade stainless steel and comes in Brushed Stainless or powder-coated Matte Black. The panels are 12mm tempered glass.

settings.question: How do I make a warranty claim?
settings.answer: Contact us at claims@glassrailingstore.com with your order details.

settings.question: Which installations are covered by the engineering documents?
settings.answer: Top mount spigots on concrete and on wood, and side mount spigots on concrete and on wood. Each set has a testing document and a blocking details document.

settings.question: Do I still need to check my local building code?
settings.answer: Ensure compliance with local building codes before you order and install.

settings.question: What tools are required to perform an installation?
settings.answer: Installing a glass railing system typically requires basic tools such as a drill, level, measuring tape, wrench set, rubber mallet, and safety equipment. Exact tools may vary depending on the surface and railing system used.

settings.question: How far apart should the spigots be?
settings.answer: Mark spigot positions at a maximum of 36 inches apart along the top edge of your deck frame or concrete surface. In our installation guide each glass panel slides into two spigots.

settings.question: How long does an installation take?
settings.answer: Our installation how-to estimates about 4 hours for a standard installation. Larger decks, stairs and gates take longer.

settings.question: Do you offer installation services?
settings.answer: We currently offer installation services exclusively in Ontario. Everywhere else, our systems are designed for DIY installation with our installation guide and videos.

settings.question: Do glass railings have to meet the building code?
settings.answer: Yes. Glass railings have to meet the building code where they are installed: national codes set the baseline, and provinces, states and municipalities can add their own requirements.

settings.question: Where can I find the code for my province or state?
settings.answer: See the Canadian Building Code and American Building Code pages, which link to each province and state guide.

settings.question: Do you have engineering documents?
settings.answer: Yes. See our engineering documents.

settings.answer: Orders are processed in 2–3 business days, including crating your glass at our warehouse, then delivered in 5–10 business days across Canada and the U.S. Custom glass is processed in 2–3 business days, then shipped in 2–3 weeks.

settings.answer: Yes. The carrier delivers the crated glass with a tailgate service. Free shipping for glass railing orders over $3,000. The price displayed at checkout is the final price with no hidden fees, tariffs, or duties, even if the order crosses borders between the US and Canada.

settings.question: What is the International Building Code (IBC)?
settings.answer: The International Building Code (IBC) is a comprehensive set of standards developed by the International Code Council (ICC) to ensure public health, safety, and welfare in building construction. The IBC is widely adopted across the United States, with states and localities often modifying it to address specific regional needs.

settings.question: Does every state use the same building code for glass railings?
settings.answer: Each state in the USA may adopt the IBC with modifications or develop its own building codes that include specific provisions for glass railings.

settings.question: Do local building codes apply to glass railings?
settings.answer: In addition to national and state codes, local municipalities often have specific building codes and regulations that apply to glass railings. It is essential to consult with local building departments to ensure compliance with any additional requirements that may apply to your project.

settings.question: What thickness of glass is used in your railings?
settings.answer:
Our glass panels are 12mm (1/2 inch) tempered glass, about double the thickness of an average car window. 12mm is the minimum many building codes set for frameless glass railings, so check the rules where you live on our building code pages.

The panels come 33.6", 39.6", 46" and 57.7" high, for 36", 42", 48" and 60" railings. See all glass railing panels.

settings.question: What materials are used in your glass railing systems?
settings.answer:
Our spigots, the 6" Engineered Spigot and the Side Mount / Fascia Spigot, are made from 2205 marine-grade stainless steel, designed to resist rust in even the harshest conditions. Our hardware comes in Brushed Stainless or Matte Black and is covered by our 10-year no-rust promise.

Read 2205 vs 316 stainless steel to see how it compares.

settings.question: Do you offer different finishes for the hardware?
settings.answer: Brushed Stainless and Matte Black.

settings.question: Are your glass panels tempered for safety?
settings.answer: Yes, glass railings are very safe when properly designed and installed. They are made from tempered safety glass, which is strong, impact-resistant, and built to meet building code requirements while providing secure protection and clear views.

settings.question: What glass sizes work for residential decks?
settings.answer: Residential decks typically use 12mm tempered glass panels, which provide the required strength and safety. Panel width and height depend on deck layout, post spacing, and local building codes, ensuring a secure fit and clean, modern appearance.

settings.question: Can I customize the size of my glass railing?
settings.answer: Yes, custom sizes are available to help fit your specific railing project requirements.

settings.question: What is the difference between the big and small glass connectors?
settings.answer: There's no functional difference between them. Both offer the same quality and the same holding power, and both are used with 12mm glass panels. The only difference is the look and design, so it comes down to which style you prefer.
